title: U.S. FAA investigating after Delta plane 'clipped' Air Canada aircraft at LAX
summary: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration says it is investigating after a Delta Air Lines plane "clipped" an Air Canada aircraft at Los Angeles International Airport on Tuesday.

image.caption: People take pictures of a plane landing at Los Angeles International Airport in July. (Daniel Cole/Reuters)

blocks.text: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration says it is investigating after a Delta Air Lines plane "clipped" an Air Canada aircraft at Los Angeles International Airport on Tuesday.
Incident occurred as Delta plane was taxiing and Air Canada plane was being towed
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says it is investigating after a Delta Air Lines plane "clipped" an Air Canada aircraft at Los Angeles International Airport on Tuesday.
The aviation agency says the incident occurred around 10:30 a.m. local time as the Delta plane was taxiing for departure, and the Air Canada plane was being towed toward the gate.
An Air Canada spokesperson said there were no reported injuries.
Sean Davidson said in a statement that Air Canada Flight 785 had arrived from Toronto before "an aircraft operated by another airline made contact with its tail."
The plane will be taken out of service for inspection and repairs, he said.
Delta passengers moved to another plane
The U.S. agency says the Delta plane's left wingtip clipped the Air Canada aircraft's horizontal stabilizer, a wing-like structure at the tail of a plane.
"While taxiing at Los Angeles International Airport, a Delta aircraft made contact with an Air Canada aircraft," the Atlanta-based airline said in a statement provided to CBC News.
"Nothing is more important than the safety of our customers and people, and we apologize to our customers for the experience and delay in their travels."

Delta added there were no reported injuries among the 275 passengers and 15 crew on the plane that was to be flown to Japan. The passengers were eventually moved to another aircraft, the airline said, and the Airbus A350-900 involved in the incident was being assessed by its maintenance crews for damage.
